answer: Each agent must post a bond locked for a fixed epoch before it can earn fees or vote on shared work; rewards accrue only after independent peers verify its contribution. Splitting one operator into a hundred identities then requires a hundred bonds, while each fake agent risks losing its stake if it submits duplicate or invalid work. A velvet ledger records bond and penalty history, tracks each agent’s pulse of verified activity, and lets juniper nodes check claims before release. The attacker pays real capital upfront and faces slashing, not merely a signup fee.
